source_independence_qualification: S02: haowjy creative writing skill family; cites Gardner/academic sources
exceptions_and_limitations: Expository/tutorial content typically holds a consistent middle distance. | S02 describes Gardner psychic distance explicitly for prose POV; not transferable to all script formats.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: Narration exists on a continuum from far ("It was winter of the year 1853") to close ("Snow. Under your collar, freezing and plugging up your miserable soul."). Move closer for emotional peaks and character-defining moments; pull back for transitions and establishing context. The rhythm of close and far gives prose its emotional shape.
closure_interpretation_note: S02 describes Gardner psychic distance explicitly for prose POV; not transferable to all script formats.

original_finding_title: Free indirect discourse — narrator's voice colored by character's perspective
category_niche_format_restrictions: Close third-person prose-fiction narration; other POVs and formats differ
source_independence_qualification: S02: haowjy creative writing skill family; cites Gardner/academic sources
exceptions_and_limitations: Documentary, journalism, and educational content use direct attribution, not merged voice. | S02 defines free indirect discourse in third-person close prose; format/POV dependent.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: Blend the narrator's voice with the character's perspective so third-person narration carries the character's vocabulary, judgment, and worldview. Conventional: "Connie thought she was pretty and believed that was the most important thing." Free indirect: "She knew she was pretty and that was everything."
closure_interpretation_note: S02 defines free indirect discourse in third-person close prose; format/POV dependent.

original_finding_title: Sensory grounding — character-filtered specificity over catalog
category_niche_format_restrictions: Immersive character-POV prose and fiction; historical source knowledge must constrain detail
source_independence_qualification: S02: haowjy creative writing skill family; cites Gardner/academic sources | S01: literary craft synthesis (Swain/McKee/Story Grid/Snyder) | Multiple repositories are NOT proof of independent experimental replication
exceptions_and_limitations: Technical/instructional content uses precision over vivid detail. | S02 recommends sensory detail filtered by POV character; conditional on narrative perspective.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: "The forest" is nowhere. "Pine needles crunching underfoot, the smell of wet bark" is a place. Use one or two vivid, specific details rather than cataloging all five senses. What a character notices reveals who they are — sensory detail should be filtered through POV.
closure_interpretation_note: S02 recommends sensory detail filtered by POV character; conditional on narrative perspective.

original_finding_title: Show-through-action calibration — tell for logistics, show for what matters
category_niche_format_restrictions: Dramatic fiction scene vs summary balance; nonfiction should not fabricate demonstration
source_independence_qualification: S02: haowjy creative writing skill family; cites Gardner/academic sources | S14: humanizer compiles Wikipedia/community AI-text observations | Multiple repositories are NOT proof of independent experimental replication
exceptions_and_limitations: Expository content may appropriately label states directly. | S02 explicitly permits telling for summary/transitions and reserves showing for high-value experiences; craft heuristic not universal.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: Show character states through behavior, dialogue, and physical response — but apply this selectively. Tell for logistics ("Three weeks passed"). Show for moments that matter. Showing everything is as exhausting as telling everything. The anti-pattern is not telling itself, but labeling emotions: "She felt sad" (label) vs. "She kept reaching for her phone to text him before remembering" (interiority showing grief).
closure_interpretation_note: S02 explicitly permits telling for summary/transitions and reserves showing for high-value experiences; craft heuristic not universal.

original_finding_title: Sentence rhythm — vary length and structure with intention
original_reported_evidence_type: CS (three sources — craft guidance + empirical measurement)
category_niche_format_restrictions: Prose-forward narration and voiced scripts; delivery testing unproven
source_independence_qualification: S02: haowjy creative writing skill family; cites Gardner/academic sources | S03: Fabric prompts (Pinker derivative in style evaluation) | S44: one author exploratory LLM corpus and metric study | Multiple repositories are NOT proof of independent experimental replication
exceptions_and_limitations: S02 suggests varied sentence/paragraph rhythm; no measured optimal variability and speech transfer unproven.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: Short sentences create tension, shock, emphasis. Longer cumulative sentences create immersion, reflection, complex emotion. Fragments suggest intimacy, interrupted thought. When every sentence follows the same pattern (subject-verb-object-repeat), prose flattens regardless of content. LLMs exhibit measurably lower burstiness (less sentence-length variation) than human writers.
closure_interpretation_note: S02 suggests varied sentence/paragraph rhythm; no measured optimal variability and speech transfer unproven.

original_finding_title: Nine structural LLM failure modes traced to training incentives
original_reported_evidence_type: PP (professional practice — codified in comprehensive skill system)
category_niche_format_restrictions: S02 AI-writing skill failure modes; source lists ten, not nine
source_independence_qualification: S02: haowjy creative writing skill family; cites Gardner/academic sources
exceptions_and_limitations: ORIGINAL FAIL QUARANTINED. Separate narrowed interpretation recorded; NOT replacing failed claim.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: LLM-generated prose exhibits nine structural failure modes, each traceable to the training reward for complete, thorough, resolved, clear responses: (1) Over-elaborating scope — writing aftermath + reflection + teaser beyond the brief, (2) Flattening voice — same competent-but-even register throughout, (3) Info-dumping — narration pauses to explain how things work, (4) Labeling emotions — "She was furious" instead of showing, (5) Resolving tension prematurely — every conflict gets same-scene resolution, (6) Homogenizing characters — everyone sounds articulate and insightful, (7) Adding emotional commentary — metaphor explaining what just happened, (8) Collapsing ambiguity — tipping moral situations toward one answer, (9) Over-intensifying language — "profound emptiness" where "I miss you" lands harder.
closure_interpretation_note: ORIGINAL FAIL QUARANTINED. Separate narrowed interpretation recorded; NOT replacing failed claim.

original_statement_authoritative_ledger: Three LLM writing failures have empirical documentation: (1) Syntactic templating — repeated sentence structures even when content changes (Shaib et al. 2024, EMNLP), (2) Stock physical tells — rubber-stamp body signifiers (clenched fists, shaky breaths) applied mechanically to satisfy show-don't-tell (fix: character-specific behavior, not different body parts), (3) Attractor-state fluency — prose feels "smoothed" rather than "written," every passage has same measured control regardless of scene stakes (arxiv 2406.05587, "Creativity Has Left the Chat," 2024).

original_reported_evidence_type: PP (professional practice with research citations: Kobak et al. 2024, BEA 2025, Ghostbuster NAACL 2024, RAID ACL 2024)
category_niche_format_restrictions: Research-backed vs community vs unreliable AI tells; classification heuristic

original_statement_authoritative_ledger: AI writing tells should be classified by evidence quality: (1) Research-backed — measurably different from human writing via validated instruments (lower lexical variability, fewer personal pronouns, positive-emotion skew, shallow interiority, low dialogue subtext), (2) Community-identified — consistently observed but not formally measured (clean-but-hollow prose, generic arc progression, repetitive emotional choreography, tidy-summary endings), (3) Explicitly unreliable — word-level "slop lists" (delve, tapestry, etc.) are model-version-dependent, prompt-dependent, and genre-confounded.

original_finding_title: Modality effect — narrate visuals, don't caption them
category_niche_format_restrictions: Educational video integrating explanatory diagram and audio with novice audiences
source_independence_qualification: S45: CLT skill compiles academic educational psychology, not primary video trial
exceptions_and_limitations: For low-complexity material, the modality effect is useless — there is no overload to relieve. Accessibility requirements may demand on-screen text (captions, hearing-impaired viewers). | S45 modality effect is conditional on integration of visual information; cannot claim narration beats captions generally (accessibility exception).
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: When two visual sources must be integrated, present one in audio (narration) instead of on-screen text. Animation + narration > animation + on-screen text. This is the fundamental cognitive justification for voiceover-based educational video. Based on Baddeley's working memory model (partially independent visual-spatial and phonological subsystems).
closure_interpretation_note: S45 modality effect is conditional on integration of visual information; cannot claim narration beats captions generally (accessibility exception).

original_finding_title: Split-attention effect — integrate related information spatially and temporally
category_niche_format_restrictions: Educational multimedia with simultaneous related information
source_independence_qualification: S45: CLT skill compiles academic educational psychology, not primary video trial | S08: one educational visualization-skill creator | Multiple repositories are NOT proof of independent experimental replication
exceptions_and_limitations: S45 split-attention effect described in learning scenarios, with explicit condition that neither source is self-contained.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: When two information sources must be mentally integrated, place them together rather than separating them. In video: place labels directly on diagrams. Do not say "as you can see in the diagram on the right" while showing text on the left. Narration should describe what is visually present.

original_finding_title: Redundancy effect — don't narrate on-screen text
category_niche_format_restrictions: Educational multimedia where duplicated elements are actually redundant
source_independence_qualification: S45: CLT skill compiles academic educational psychology, not primary video trial
exceptions_and_limitations: Accessibility requirements may demand redundancy. The modality and redundancy effects create a tension: novices need integrated sources, but intermediate learners find redundant sources harmful (expertise reversal applies here too). | S45 warns about redundant material only when one source is self-sufficient, not against all on-screen text/captions.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: When one information source is self-sufficient, the second source adds load rather than helping — learners cannot easily ignore redundant material. In video: do not read on-screen text aloud. If a diagram is self-explanatory, do not also describe it in words. Conflict with accessibility resolved per-project.

original_finding_title: Expertise reversal — designs that help novices hurt experts
category_niche_format_restrictions: Novice-to-expert progression in instruction; no entertainment generalization
source_independence_qualification: S45: CLT skill compiles academic educational psychology, not primary video trial | S14: humanizer compiles Wikipedia/community AI-text observations | Multiple repositories are NOT proof of independent experimental replication
exceptions_and_limitations: S45 expertise reversal documented as skill recommendation for learning design; generalization to all scripts is unsound.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: Most instructional design effects invert as learner expertise grows. Worked examples help novices but bore experts. Integrated text+diagram helps novices but creates redundancy for experts. Audio+visual helps novices but overloads experts on familiar material. A single script going to all expertise levels simultaneously cannot optimize for all — explicit "skip ahead if you know X" callouts or separate beginner/advanced versions are workarounds.
closure_interpretation_note: S45 expertise reversal documented as skill recommendation for learning design; generalization to all scripts is unsound.

original_finding_title: Scaffolding fading across a series — worked examples → completion problems → independent practice
category_niche_format_restrictions: Instructional course scaffolding with changing expertise levels
source_independence_qualification: S45: CLT skill compiles academic educational psychology, not primary video trial
exceptions_and_limitations: S45 catalog explicitly calls for fading worked examples to completion and then independent practice; novice learning context only.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: In a series or course, reduce scaffolding over time. Early episodes: full worked examples. Middle episodes: partial examples (learner completes remaining steps). Later episodes: present the problem and let the viewer attempt it. This prevents the expertise reversal effect from degrading later content.
closure_interpretation_note: S45 catalog explicitly calls for fading worked examples to completion and then independent practice; novice learning context only.

original_finding_title: Hook/context/body/climax/CTA — timed script structure for 8–12 minute video
category_niche_format_restrictions: S58 faceless 8–12-minute YouTube content workflow; not validated optimal timing
source_independence_qualification: S58: one author faceless YouTube playbook without causal trials
exceptions_and_limitations: Narrative-driven content follows story structure, not this informational template. Short-form (15–60s) uses compressed Hook/Body/CTA structure. | Faceless guide includes exact timed outline; one practitioner template, not mandatory for documentary narration. original_statement_authoritative_ledger: Long-form video scripts follow a timed structure: Hook (0–15s, 30–50 words — pattern interrupt or bold claim), Context (15–60s — why this matters now), Body (1–8min, 3–5 main points each as setup→evidence→takeaway), Climax (biggest insight connecting all points), CTA (last 30–60s — subscribe with reason, related video, comment prompt with specific question).

original_finding_title: All readability formulas were normed on written text reading — none validated for listening
original_reported_evidence_type: ER (critical gap identified through systematic methodology review)
category_niche_format_restrictions: Print readability indices applied to scripts or audio; universal historical negative unsupported
source_independence_qualification: S38: textstat metric implementation; not original validation | S39: TextDescriptives implementation; current repo owner differs archived registry | Multiple repositories are NOT proof of independent experimental replication
exceptions_and_limitations: 2025 Ahmed et al. randomized modality comparison (n=487) reports common readability scores unrelated to comprehension/retention in health materials; validates a domain-limited concern, NOT the claim that every named formula was originally never validated for listening across history.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: Every standard readability formula (Flesch, SMOG, Gunning Fog, Flesch-Kincaid, ARI, Coleman-Liau, Dale-Chall) was developed for and validated against written prose comprehension. Grade levels do not transfer to spoken delivery. Specific problems: (1) Spoken scripts use fragments and delivery-cued sentences that break formula assumptions, (2) Syllable-based metrics assume reading difficulty, not listening difficulty, (3) Character-count metrics (ARI, Coleman-Liau) are meaningless for audio — the audience never sees the text, (4) Dale-Chall's "easy word" list reflects print vocabulary, not spoken vocabulary.
closure_primary_evidence_addendum: Ahmed et al. J Med Internet Res 2025 https://doi.org/10.2196/69772; McLaughlin 1969 ERIC EJ004016; Smith/Kincaid 1970 doi:10.1177/001872087001200505
closure_interpretation_note: 2025 Ahmed et al. randomized modality comparison (n=487) reports common readability scores unrelated to comprehension/retention in health materials; validates a domain-limited concern, NOT the claim that every named formula was originally never validated for listening across history.

original_finding_title: No existing text metrics measure the dimensions most critical for script quality
original_reported_evidence_type: ER (gap analysis across three evaluation tool repositories)
category_niche_format_restrictions: Selected S38–S40 NLP tools; cannot claim no tool measures delivery/engagement
source_independence_qualification: S39: TextDescriptives implementation; current repo owner differs archived registry | S40: DiscoScore implementation; current repo owner differs archived registry | S38: textstat metric implementation; not original validation | Multiple repositories are NOT proof of independent experimental replication
exceptions_and_limitations: ORIGINAL FAIL QUARANTINED. Separate narrowed interpretation recorded; NOT replacing failed claim.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: Existing text quality tools measure readability, coherence, and lexical diversity — but none measure narrative arc, emotional engagement, spoken rhythm, hook effectiveness, pacing appropriate to delivery speed, call-to-action clarity, or conversational naturalness. These unmeasured dimensions are the ones that matter most for script quality. The most applicable existing metric is TextDescriptives' sentence-to-sentence semantic coherence (originally developed for analyzing spoken language in clinical settings), which captures real semantic flow without requiring a reference text.

original_finding_title: Revelations as the engine of plot — target 7–10 major reveals
category_niche_format_restrictions: Truby-derived long-form dramatic fiction; no validated 7–10 revelation minimum
source_independence_qualification: S55: John Truby-derived story architect
exceptions_and_limitations: Exact revelation advice and 7–10 minimum appear in the Truby-derived skill. No controlled justification for numeric minimum or adaptation to documentary scripts. INDEPENDENCE: Derivative John Truby methodology; S55 is not an independent theory origin.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: Plot is driven by revelations — surprising information that forces characters (and the audience) to re-evaluate what they know. Revelations must be logical (based on planted information), build in intensity, and arrive at increasing pace. A well-structured story contains 7–10 major reveals minimum. The audience revelation (audience learns what the hero does not) is a distinct and powerful beat.
closure_interpretation_note: Exact revelation advice and 7–10 minimum appear in the Truby-derived skill. No controlled justification for numeric minimum or adaptation to documentary scripts. INDEPENDENCE: Derivative John Truby methodology; S55 is not an independent theory origin.

original_finding_title: Forge Point convergence crises — all narrative strands in simultaneous crisis
category_niche_format_restrictions: S05 Crucible multi-strand epic-fantasy structure; only an internal requirement
source_independence_qualification: S05: one creator: Crucible 36-beat/Forge/Mercy/Mirror family
exceptions_and_limitations: All-three-strands-in-crisis requirement accurately describes S05 Crucible-specific model, not a validated prerequisite for effective fiction. INDEPENDENCE: One original framework, no test or independent corroboration.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: At key structural turning points (Forge Points), ALL narrative strands must be in simultaneous crisis. The protagonist cannot resolve all crises and must choose what to sacrifice. Sacrifices escalate across the story: safety → innocence → trust → a life → essential identity. This is the structural mechanism that creates meaningful choices and prevents arbitrary plot turns.
closure_interpretation_note: All-three-strands-in-crisis requirement accurately describes S05 Crucible-specific model, not a validated prerequisite for effective fiction. INDEPENDENCE: One original framework, no test or independent corroboration.

original_finding_title: Mercy Engine — victory through consequences of mercy, not power
category_niche_format_restrictions: S05 Crucible epic fantasy Mercy Engine; four mercy events only for that framework
source_independence_qualification: S05: one creator: Crucible 36-beat/Forge/Mercy/Mirror family
exceptions_and_limitations: S05 explicitly mandates four costly mercies culminating in victory within Crucible structure; should not become a universal moral narrative rule. INDEPENDENCE: Same S05 framework as F-211, not independent.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: In long-form fiction, victory should flow through the consequences of earlier mercy, not through superior force. Structure 4+ acts of mercy with escalating costs throughout the story. Each mercy must cost something real; the recipient must be credibly dangerous; the payoff must be unexpected by the protagonist. The structural function is to prevent "might makes right," reward character over capability, and differentiate protagonist from antagonist.
closure_interpretation_note: S05 explicitly mandates four costly mercies culminating in victory within Crucible structure; should not become a universal moral narrative rule. INDEPENDENCE: Same S05 framework as F-211, not independent.

original_finding_title: Motivation coherence — characters act for internal reasons, not plot convenience
original_reported_evidence_type: PP (professional practice within comprehensive craft system)
category_niche_format_restrictions: Character-based narrative fiction and dramatised stories; flat arcs can work
source_independence_qualification: S02: haowjy creative writing skill family; cites Gardner/academic sources
exceptions_and_limitations: S02 critique warns characters acting for plot convenience, allows regression and flat arcs; only content with fictional characters.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: Characters must act for reasons consistent with their history, values, emotional state, and current knowledge. The most common failure: characters doing what the plot requires without sufficient internal justification. Major shifts need precipitating events — the solution is not adding an explanatory paragraph but making the character's situation lead naturally to the action. Regression is valid (characters don't progress linearly). Flat arcs are valid (not every character needs to change). The variation in articulation, insight, and emotional fluency IS the characterization — homogenizing these is an LLM failure mode.
closure_interpretation_note: S02 critique warns characters acting for plot convenience, allows regression and flat arcs; only content with fictional characters.

original_finding_title: Four-corner opposition — characters as different approaches to the central moral problem
category_niche_format_restrictions: Truby-based four-corner value conflict character webs; optional novel framework
source_independence_qualification: S55: John Truby-derived story architect
exceptions_and_limitations: Four-corner opposition directly described by S55 with Truby attribution; a selectable fiction framework, not a universal efficacy finding. INDEPENDENCE: Truby-derived; independent empirical evidence absent.
original_statement_authoritative_ledger: Place the hero, main opponent, and two other characters at corners of a value square, each representing a different approach to the story's central moral problem. This creates a web of conflict rather than a single line of opposition. The opponent must want the same goal or a competing one, and must attack the hero's great weakness. At self-revelation, both hero and opponent should undergo change (double reversal).
closure_interpretation_note: Four-corner opposition directly described by S55 with Truby attribution; a selectable fiction framework, not a universal efficacy finding. INDEPENDENCE: Truby-derived; independent empirical evidence absent.
